questions.stem: In a preterm baby with Respiratory distress syndrome, which type of cell is deficient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Type 2 alveolar cell

In a preterm baby with Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS), the deficiency occurs in Type 2 alveolar cells. These cells are responsible for producing surfactant, a substance that reduces surface tension in the alveoli (air sacs) of the lungs, preventing their collapse during exhalation.



Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition Page no. 611, 620., Nelson Textbook of Pediatrics 20th Edition Page:- 851, Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 31st edition Page :- 229-230, 234

questions.stem: A young man met with a motor bike accident and had injury to ileum and jejunum. Therefore the entire ileum and partial jejunum was resected. Which of the following would the patient suffer from?
questions.solutionHtml:
Vitamin B12 deficiency
  • The patient would suffer from Vitamin B12 deficiency (option A) after the resection of the entire ileum and partial jejunum. Vitamin B12 is primarily absorbed in the ileum, along with other nutrients.
  • The absence or removal of the ileum can lead to impaired absorption of Vitamin B12 from the diet, resulting in a deficiency over time.


Ganong's Review Of Medical physiology, 26th Edition Page no:470, 478.

questions.stem: The reflex in which there is inhibition of gastric emptying when there is acid and hypertonic solution in the duodenum:
questions.solutionHtml:
Enterogastric
  • The reflex that inhibits gastric emptying when there is acid and hypertonic solution in the duodenum is known as the enterogastric reflex (option A).
  • When the duodenum detects the presence of acid or hypertonicity, it sends signals to the stomach via the enterogastric reflex to slow down gastric emptying. This reflex helps to regulate the rate at which food leaves the stomach and enters the small intestine, allowing for proper digestion and absorption.


Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 13th Edition Page no. 811 and 812.

questions.stem: In multiple sclerosis, slow conduction of motor and sensory pathway is due to:

questions.stem: Water hammer pulse is seen in:
questions.solutionHtml:
Aortic regurgitation
  • Water hammer pulse, also known as Corrigan's pulse, is a characteristic pulsation of the arteries that has a rapid and forceful upstroke followed by a quick collapse. This pulse is seen in: Aortic regurgitation

questions.stem: A boy met with an motor Bike Accident. CT brain shows injury to posterior end of superior temporal gyrus. He is likely to suffer from:
questions.solutionHtml:
Fluent aphasia

Based on the location of the brain injury described in the CT scan (posterior end of the superior temporal gyrus), the boy is likely to suffer from Wernicke's aphasia, which is a type of fluent aphasia.

  • The superior temporal gyrus contains the primary auditory cortex, which is responsible for processing sounds
  • It includes Wernicke's area, which is the major area involved in the comprehension of language.


Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine 20th Edition Page no 159

questions.stem: The lab reports of a patient given below ph=7.2HCO3=10mEq/lPCO2=30 mmhgThis exemplifies which of the following disorder:
questions.solutionHtml:
Metabolic acidosis

Metabolic acidosis occurs when there is an excess of acid in the body or a decrease in the level of bicarbonate. In this case, the low pH and low bicarbonate levels indicate metabolic acidosis.



Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine 20th Edition Page no 315, Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 13th Edition Page no 422, Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 21st Edition Page no 365

questions.stem: In which of the following conditions would the Cortisol level be highest?

options.label: C
options.text: Normal person after wakening in morning

questions.answerText: Normal person after wakening in morning
questions.solutionHtml:
Normal person after wakening in morning

Cortisol follows a diurnal pattern, which means its levels naturally fluctuate throughout the day. In a normal person, cortisol levels are typically highest in the early morning, shortly after waking up. This is known as the "Cortisol awakening response" and occurs to help prepare the body for the day's activities.



Ganong Textbook of physiology 26th edition Page no 421, Ganong Textbook of physiology 24th edition Page no. 368.

questions.stem: Blood stored in citrate- Phosphate-dextrose is better for hypoxic patients, than acid- citrate- dextrose because?

options.label: C
options.text: The fall in 2, 3 DBG is less

questions.answerText: The fall in 2, 3 DBG is less
questions.solutionHtml:
The fall in 2, 3 DBG is less
  • Citrate-Phosphate-Dextrose (CPD) is commonly used as alkaline PH and Phosphate help in maintaining 2,3 DBG.
  • 2,3-diphosphoglycerate (2,3-DPG or 2,3-DPG) is a molecule found in red blood cells that plays a crucial role in the delivery of oxygen to tissues. It binds to hemoglobin and reduces its affinity for oxygen, allowing hemoglobin to release oxygen more easily in tissues with low oxygen levels (hypoxic conditions).


Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition Page no: 611.

questions.stem: When VA/Q is infinity, it means:

options.label: B
options.text: The po2 of alveolar air is 159 mmHg and pco2 is 40 mmHg

options.label: C
options.text: Partial pressure of O2 and Co2 are equal

questions.solutionHtml:
Dead space

When VA/Q (ventilation-perfusion ratio) is infinity, it means that the ventilation (V) is infinite while the perfusion (Q) is absent or negligible. In other words, there is air ventilation without any blood flow to the alveoli.



Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition Page no 624. Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology - 25th Edition Page no 632 and 633.

questions.stem: C wave in JVP is due to:

options.label: A
options.text: Bulging of tricuspid valve during the isovolumetric contraction phase

questions.answerText: Bulging of tricuspid valve during the isovolumetric contraction phase
questions.solutionHtml:
Bulging of tricuspid valve during the isovolumetric contraction phase
  • During the isovolumetric contraction phase, the ventricles are contracting, but the semilunar valves (aortic and pulmonic valves) are still closed. As the ventricles contract, the pressure within the ventricles increases.
  • This increased pressure causes the tricuspid valve, which lies between the right atrium and right ventricle, to bulge backward into the right atrium. This bulging of the tricuspid valve into the right atrium creates a temporary increase in jugular venous pressure, leading to the C wave in the JVP waveform.


Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 21st Edition Page 1817. Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine 20th Edition Page no. 1573. Ganong's Review Of Medical physiology, 26th Edition Page no 531

questions.stem: Impaired function of aquaporin results in?
questions.solutionHtml:
Nephrogenic DI
  • Mutation or functional deficiency of aquaporin-2 causes nephrogenic diabetes insipidus.
  • in NDI, the impaired aquaporins prevent this reabsorption, resulting in the excretion of large volumes of dilute urine. As a consequence, affected individuals experience excessive thirst (polydipsia) and excessive urination (polyuria) with a low concentration of urine.


Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine 20th Edition Page no: 302, 303

questions.stem: Vitamin B12 is found in?
questions.solutionHtml:
Animal products

Vitamin B12 is primarily found in animal products. It is not naturally present in significant amounts in plant-based foods.



Ganong's Review Of Medical physiology, 26th Edition Page no:470, 478.

questions.stem: A 50 year old man present with paresthesia. Hb=6.8 gms/dl. Peripheral smear shows macrocytes and neutrophils with hypersegmented nuclei. Endoscopy reveals atrophic gastritis. Which of the following deficiency is more likely?
questions.solutionHtml:
Vitamin B12 deficiency
  • Hb-6.8 -> anaemia
  • Macrocytes and Hypersegmented neutrophil-> Megaloblastic anaemia -> either due to Folic acid or Vit. B12 deficiency
  • Atrophic gastritis-> atrophy of parietal cells->
  • Decreased IF secretion-> so decreased Vit. B12 absorption, Thus in the given scenario Vit. B12 deficiency is more likely.


Ganong's Review Of Medical physiology, 26th Edition Page no:470, 478.

questions.stem: Which of the following binds to the Tyrosine kinase receptor?
questions.solutionHtml:
Insulin

  • The insulin receptor is a type of receptor known as a receptor tyrosine kinase.
